beats.intro: Learning module one. [[sub]]What a derivative is, what it is built on, and where it trades.
beats.spot: [[spot]]In a spot market, also called a cash market, an asset changes hands now, at today's price, the spot price. [[deriv]]A derivative is different. Two parties agree today on an exchange that happens in the future. [[value]]And the value of that agreement is derived from something else, the underlying.
beats.forward: [[boxes]]Here is a simple example: a forward contract. [[t0]]Today, A M Y Investments agrees to sell one thousand Airbus shares to a financial intermediary, in six months, at thirty euros a share. No money changes hands yet. [[tT]]Six months later, the deal settles. A M Y delivers the shares and receives thirty thousand euros. [[st]]Suppose the share price has fallen to twenty-five euros. The shares are worth only twenty-five thousand. [[gain]]A M Y still gets thirty thousand, five thousand more than the market would pay. [[cash]]The two sides could also just settle the five thousand euro difference in cash. [[risk]]A M Y has transferred its price risk to the counterparty. And that brings a new risk: will the counterparty pay? That is counterparty credit risk.
beats.terms: [[sheet]]Every derivative is a legal agreement with the same basic features. [[f1]]The underlying: the asset or variable the value comes from. [[f2]]The counterparties: the legal entities on each side. [[f3]]The maturity: when the contract settles. [[f4]]And the contract size, or notional amount. [[f5]]The buyer gains when the underlying rises, like a long position. The seller is exposed like a short position.
beats.types: [[firm]]Derivatives come in two families. In a firm commitment, both parties must exchange a pre-agreed amount at settlement. [[firmEx]]Forwards, futures and swaps are firm commitments. [[cont]]In a contingent claim, one party decides whether, and when, the trade settles. [[contEx]]The option is the main contingent claim. [[embed]]A derivative can stand alone, like our forward. Or it can be embedded inside another security, like the call feature in a callable bond.
beats.why: [[head]]Why use a derivative at all? Derivative markets widen the set of opportunities. [[u1]]Investors can sell short, and benefit from a fall in price. [[u2]]They can diversify a portfolio. [[u3]]Issuers can offset the market exposure of a commercial deal. [[u4]]Large exposures can be created with a small cash outlay. [[u5]]And costs are often lower, with more liquidity than the spot market. [[hedge]]Using a derivative to offset an existing or expected exposure is called hedging. The derivative is the hedge.
beats.underlyings: [[head]]Derivatives are grouped by their underlying. [[u1]]Equities: single stocks, stock indexes, even equity volatility. Stock options are also used to pay employees. [[u2]]Fixed income and interest rates: bonds, and market reference rates like SOFR. [[u3]]Currencies, used to hedge foreign exchange risk in trade and investing. [[u4]]Commodities: soft ones like corn and cattle, hard ones like oil and metals. [[u5]]Credit: credit default swaps transfer the risk of a borrower's default. [[u6]]And others, such as weather, cryptocurrencies and longevity.
beats.scenarios: [[hi]]Two scenarios. Hightest Capital expects health care stocks to beat the market over six months. [[hiDeal]]It buys an option on a health care stock index: the right to buy the index at five percent above today's level, in six months. That is a contingent claim. [[es]]Esterr has a 250 million Canadian dollar floating-rate loan, paying the market reference rate plus one point five percent. [[esFear]]Its treasurer fears rising rates. [[swap]]So Esterr enters an interest rate swap. It pays a fixed rate, two point oh five percent, and receives the floating rate. [[net]]The floating payments cancel. Esterr's cost is now fixed at three point five five percent. That swap is a firm commitment.
beats.otc: [[net]]Where do derivatives trade? First, over the counter, or O T C. [[users]]End users, issuers and investors, deal directly with financial intermediaries, the dealers. [[dealers]]Dealers then offset their risk by trading with each other. [[custom]]O T C contracts can be customized to fit an exact exposure. [[cons]]But they are less transparent, carry more counterparty risk, and may be less liquid.
beats.etd: [[hub]]The second venue is the exchange. Exchange-traded derivatives, or E T Ds, are standardized. [[spec]]The exchange sets the terms: contract size, quality, maturity dates and settlement. [[mm]]Market makers stand ready to buy at one price and sell at a higher price, earning the bid offer spread. [[coll]]Every trader posts collateral, and the exchange guarantees against default. [[clear]]Clearing verifies the trade and records who owes what. Settlement is the final payment or delivery. [[transp]]And trades are reported in full: the market is transparent.
beats.compare: [[head]]Side by side. [[r1]]O T C contracts are customized; exchange contracts are standardized. [[r2]]O T C trades are private; exchange trades are transparent. [[r3]]O T C carries more counterparty risk; on an exchange, collateral protects both sides. [[r4]]And exchange contracts usually have lower costs and more liquidity. The trade off is flexibility.
beats.clearing: [[intro]]After the two thousand eight financial crisis, regulators required central clearing for most O T C derivatives. [[s1]]Step one. Two dealers execute a swap on a swap execution facility, or S E F. [[s2]]Step two. The trade details go to a central counterparty, the C C P. [[s3]]Step three. Novation. The C C P replaces the original trade, and becomes the counterparty to both dealers. [[good]]End users keep the flexibility of O T C contracts, while dealers get exchange-style risk control. [[risk]]The catch: credit risk is now concentrated in the C C P. If it failed, the whole system would feel it.
beats.venues: [[back]]Back to our scenarios. [[hi]]Hightest's index option has a standard size, exercise price and maturity. It most likely trades on an exchange. [[es]]Esterr's swap is tailored to its loan's dates and maturity, so it is an O T C trade. [[dealer]]The dealer hedges it on a S E F, and that trade is then novated to a C C P.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]A derivative derives its value from an underlying, and settles in the future. [[w2]]Firm commitments must be settled; contingent claims let one party choose. [[w3]]O T C contracts are customized; exchange contracts are standardized, transparent and collateralized. [[w4]]Central counterparties take on dealers' credit risk, and concentrate it.
beats.finish: That's the end of learning module one.
